{{< include _nav.qmd >}}

**A relational SQLite database of 3,001 video games (2001–2016), combining sales figures, Metacritic critic and user reviews, gameplay variables and natural-language sentiment scores.**

I built this database for my data analytics bootcamp at DataScientest (Sorbonne). It started from a Kaggle video game sales dataset, which I cleaned and reshaped so that each game is one row. I then scraped Metacritic for metascores, critic reviews, user reviews and community gameplay ratings (difficulty, play time and completion), and scored the review text with three sentiment models (VADER, TextBlob and a Hugging Face transformer). The result is normalised into 13 linked tables.

Everything is in one file, so it can be opened directly with Python's built-in `sqlite3` module, [DB Browser for SQLite](https://sqlitebrowser.org/), DBeaver or any tool that reads SQLite.

## Downloads

| Download | Contents |
|:--|:--|
| [SQLite database — video_games.db](downloads/video-games/video_games.db) | 13 tables: games, platforms, critics, users, 15,356 critic reviews, 8,593 user reviews, ratings, sentiment scores, gameplay variables and sales. About 10 MB. |
| [Flat file — one row per game, CSV](downloads/video-games/video_game_vars_plus_sentiment_metrics.csv) | 3,001 rows. Sales, year, genre, publisher, developer, platforms, metascore, gameplay variables, review counts and the sentiment metrics, merged into a single table for quick analysis. |

All of the files, including the full raw review text with per-review sentiment scores (about 210 MB, too large to host here), are also on Kaggle: [Video Games: Gameplay, Reviews & Sentiment Scores](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aaronrmartin/video-games-gameplay-reviews-sentiment-scores).

## Tables

| Table | Rows | What it holds |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `GameID` | 3,001 | Game titles and their integer keys. |
| `PlatformID` | 19 | Platforms, from Game Boy Advance to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. |
| `CriticID` | 453 | Critic outlets. |
| `UserID` | 6,478 | Metacritic usernames. |
| `GamePlatformID` | 555 | Each game–platform combination that has reviews. |
| `CriticReviewsTable` | 15,356 | Critic review text and score, keyed to game, platform and critic. |
| `UserReviewsTable` | 8,593 | User review text and score, keyed to game, platform and user. |
| `RatingsTable` | 3,001 | Metascore, global mean user score and sampled mean user score per game. |
| `SentimentScoresTable` | 3,001 | Mean VADER, TextBlob and Hugging Face sentiment per game. |
| `CompositeSentimentScoresTable` | 3,001 | Four composite sentiment indices that weight the three models differently. |
| `GameplayTable` | 3,001 | Metacritic community votes on difficulty, play time and completion, as counts plus weighted averages. |
| `GameVarsTable` | 3,001 | Year, genre, publisher, developer, review counts and sales in North America, Europe, Japan and elsewhere (millions of units). |
| `GamePlatformSentimentTable` | 508 | Positive, mixed and negative review shares for users and critics, per game and platform. |

All tables join on `GameID`; the review tables also join on `PlatformID`, `CriticID` or `UserID`.

## Example query

```python
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

con = sqlite3.connect("video_games.db")

query = """
SELECT g.game_title, v.Year, v.Genre, v.Total_Sales,
       r.metascore, r.user_score_mean, s.vader_sentiment_mean
FROM GameID AS g
JOIN GameVarsTable AS v ON v.GameID = g.GameID
JOIN RatingsTable AS r ON r.GameID = g.GameID
JOIN SentimentScoresTable AS s ON s.GameID = g.GameID
ORDER BY v.Total_Sales DESC
LIMIT 10
"""

print(pd.read_sql_query(query, con))
```
